content: Selenium sulfide is an anti-infective medication that is prescribed to alleviate itching and flaking of the scalp. It works by removing the dry, scaly particles commonly referred to as dandruff or seborrhea. Additionally, it is used to treat tinea versicolor, a fungal infection of the skin. In some cases, this medication may be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Selenium sulfide is available as a lotion and is typically applied as a shampoo. When used as a shampoo, it is generally applied twice a week for the first two weeks, followed by once a week for two to four weeks, depending on your response to the treatment. For skin infections, it is usually applied once daily for seven days. Always follow the instructions on the package or prescription label carefully. If you have any questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Use selenium sulfide exactly as directed and do not use more or less of it, or use it more frequently than prescribed. Avoid using this medication on areas of the scalp or skin that are cut or scratched. Take care to prevent the medication from getting into your eyes. If accidental contact occurs, rinse your eyes thoroughly with clear water for several minutes. Do not leave the medication on your skin or scalp for extended periods (e.g., overnight), as it can cause irritation. Rinse off all of the lotion completely. This medication should not be used on children under two years of age without a doctor’s approval. To use the lotion as a shampoo, follow these steps: 1. Remove all jewelry, as selenium sulfide may damage it. 2. Wash your hair with regular shampoo and rinse thoroughly. 3. Shake the selenium sulfide lotion well. 4. Massage 1–2 teaspoons of the lotion into your wet scalp. 5. Leave the lotion on your scalp for 2–3 minutes. 6. Rinse your scalp three or four times with clean water. 7. Repeat steps 4, 5, and 6. 8. If you are using selenium sulfide before or after bleaching, tinting, or permanently waving your hair, rinse your hair with cool water for at least five minutes after applying the medication to prevent hair discoloration. 9. Wash your hands thoroughly and clean under your nails to remove any lotion residue. If your doctor instructs you to use the lotion on your skin, apply a small amount of water with the lotion to the affected area and massage it to form a lather. Leave the lotion on your skin for 10 minutes, then rinse it off thoroughly. Before using selenium sulfide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to selenium sulfide or any other medications. Also, let them know about all prescription and nonprescription medications, including vitamins, that you are taking. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using selenium sulfide, contact your doctor immediately. If you forget to apply a dose, do so as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Selenium sulfide may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following mild side effects and they persist or worsen: Oiliness or dryness of the hair and scalp Hair loss Hair discoloration If you experience severe side effects, such as scalp or skin irritation, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. Selenium sulfide is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not swallow it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin medications to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist. Inform your doctor if your skin condition worsens or does not improve.
